Question: What is the funniest joke you've been told that you still think about to this day?
Answer: A man goes into a pub and orders three pints all at once. He slowly drinks all three, then leaves. He does this every Friday for a month or so, when finally the barman says "Wouldn't it be better if I pour you a pint at a time, so each will be fresh when you come to drink it?" "That's sensible" says the man, half way through the first pint "except I have two brothers, one in Australia and one in Canada and I like to imagine the three of us sitting here having a drink all together" "I see" says the barman, and nothing more is said. Just after Christmas the man comes in and orders just two pints. He looks miserable, and so the barman assumes something has happened to one of the brothers. "I'm so sorry for you loss" he says. "Oh, my brothers are fine" the man says, "It's me…I'm doing dry January".

Name: Nick Schön
Question: Was the ‘Get Brexit Done’ slogan a vote-winner for the Tories in 2019? If so, then why have the Tories barely mentioned Brexit at all during the 2024 election campaign? Shouldn’t they be proudly running on the fact that they indeed got Brexit done?
Answer: A state of limbo is always uncomfortable, so in a sense whichever side of the Brexit debate you were on, you wanted change. The Conservatives owned Brexit and the fact that it hasn't turned out well (as predicted by many Brexit skeptics) is down to them. Even people who wanted Brexit say the Conservatives screwed it up (as if a lead balloon could ever fly). So of course the Conservatives aren't pointing to it as one of their great triumphs. It's a bloody disaster. Labour under Jeremy Corbyn supported this act of self-harm, and as Starmer supported Corbyn, Labour can't talk about Brexit either. They offered no opposition. Reform was UKIP, so of course they were interested only in Brexit. In their strange, upside-down world where Trump deserves their support, where climate change isn't happening and where vaccines are highly suspicious, of course Brexit is a great success. However as this view by and large isn't shared with voters, they too are not highlighting it. Dedicated hard-right voters will always vote for them so they hardly need to mention it. Anyway, it's done. So the only party of any size who has a clean track record on Brexit are the LibDems. They aren't talking about it because the debate has moved on. However some of us remember that they were the one-eyed king in the land of the blind.

Question: Why do some people refuse to use self checkout lanes in stores?

Question: What are the main differences between driving on British roads and American roads, besides left-sided traffic?
Answer: We have a lot of roundabouts. Americans call them "traffic circles" and they are not unknown there of course, but in the U.K. they are everywhere. There are even a few roundabouts arranged around a roundabout and one can travel in both directions around it. Hemel Hempstead is the proud owner of what is locally known as "The Magic Roundabout". If I were you I'd avoid that if possible or you'll get a nosebleed just trying to figure it out. I'm reliably informed by American relatives that we drive at "terrifying" speeds. Since UK roads are considerably safer than US roads and speed is a common cause of accidents, I doubt this is in fact true, but it might seem that way because our roads are so much narrower. Each lane is narrower and so vehicles are closer together. This is another issue for US drivers. Fine judgement is often called for. Where I live there are some rural roads wide enough for only one car. Meet a vehicle coming towards you and one of you will have to reverse to a slightly wider bit of road. Even then it will be a squeeze. That brings me to another point. Politeness is required. Courtesy is necessary. If someone lets you out in traffic or reverses to let you pass, it is normal to do a little wave, flash your headlights or let your hazard lights blink once to thank the other motorist. As a rule, observe what others do and copy their tone. Don't be aggressive behind the wheel. You may have to be assertive in order to make progress but don't be a dick and block junctions. Drive defensively as a rule. Err on the side of caution. Avoid using the horn. A gentle "toot" is the most that is ever needed and is quite a strong statement in the U.K. At what we call "zebra crossings" the motorist has to stop if someone is waiting to cross. School buses don't just stop in the middle of U.K. streets. They pull over to the side of the roads so the children can safely disembark. It's quite ok to pass a stationary school bus on the right. If you get pulled over by a traffic policeman you will be greeted by someone who might have had a hard day but won't be nasty or violent. You may get a telling off but usually it will be administered with good humour and certainly politeness. If you get a ticket, pay it and move on. Horses have right of way. I'm sure I've missed other points of difference. But courtesy, mimicking the tone of the other road users and not being a dick will get you quite a long way.
